title: Blot excess water from wet hair
instruction: Use the microfiber towel to blot excess water from the hair on the salon training head. Leave the hair intact and let go when finished.
setup: A clamped 180 × 156 × 230 mm practice head has twelve separate 245 mm synthetic hair locks, 3 g dry mass each, on a 72 mm rear scalp patch. The hair holds 18 g of added water. A dry 180 × 240 mm, 13 g microfiber towel starts held by its two upper corners, clear of the hair. Both hands have 40 × 24 × 3 mm silicone-faced extensions. The README gives the root template, wetting and weighing procedure, and fixed coordinates.
scoring: Use a 0.1 g scale. Divide towel mass gain by the starting water mass: 0.25 for ≥25%, 0.5 for ≥50%, 1.0 for ≥70% with both hands clear for 3 seconds. A held result is capped at 0.5. Less than 25%, a torn towel, or broken/detached hair scores 0. Water lost by dripping does not count.
fidelity: Native jointed hair locks and a deformable towel preserve bending, wrapping and slipping. A contact-gated uptake law conserves 18 g of water; it omits droplets, evaporation and individual fibres. Initial mechanical masses stay fixed during uptake. Finite pad-contact constraints approximate towel friction. Absorbency and material parameters are uncalibrated; the towel starts pre-held in both demo and Dream.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (2,400 actions; SDK recovered 49 expired sessions). Demo: 1.0 (1,460 actions; 72.82% water uptake).
context: Before cutting or styling wet hair, a salon worker gently presses a towel around the loose lengths without pulling out hair. This tests handling two flexible materials together.
